steps.eyebrow: PyRIT · agents as targets · design walkthrough
steps.lede: PyRIT can red-team an **agent**, not just a model: a harness that plans, calls tools and changes state inside an environment PyRIT owns and disposes of. One receipt, five ways.

steps.title: What you will see
steps.lede: Each chapter has one stage that evolves step by step, a claim on the left, and the code that makes it true on the right, pinned to the branch tips of the stack.

principles.title: Unchanged above the target
principles.text: Attacks, converters and scorers do not know an agent is on the other side.

principles.title: Core owns policy, providers own resources
principles.text: Two executable seams: environment and harness.

principles.title: Did, not said
principles.text: An append-only journal and an explicit projection; silence has reasons.

principles.title: Bring your own model, keep your own key
principles.text: The relay is how the model becomes a PyRIT target and how no credential enters the environment.

chapters.eyebrow: Chapter 01 · one turn, end to end
chapters.title: One turn, end to end
chapters.summary: An attack sends one message; a real agent plans, calls a tool, answers; PyRIT returns what it did.
chapters.takeaway: The thing under test is a **harness** that plans, calls tools and changes state inside an environment PyRIT owns. Existing attacks, scorers and converters run against it **unchanged**.

legend.label: Agent-owned · harness, its frames, its effects

steps.title: One turn, end to end
steps.takeaway: Follow a single message from an unchanged attack through a real agent and back. Everything on this stage is either **PyRIT-owned** (mint) or **agent-owned** (amber); the border between them is the point of the design.

steps.title: The attack does not know it is talking to an agent
steps.body: `AgentTarget` is one more `PromptTarget`. It accepts the current user message only and **never replays tool-producing history** to the harness: the agent owns its own session state.

captions.label: attack
captions.text: Any existing attack, converter chain or scorer.

captions.label: target
captions.text: Validates user text; hands the message to the execution manager.

steps.title: First message: an execution is allocated and launched
steps.body: The manager persists a record, asks the **environment provider** for a session, reserves deterministic resource identifiers, then launches the harness command with a private home. State moves `starting → idle`. Every later message in this conversation reuses the same execution.

captions.label: runtime
captions.text: `record.json` is written before any resource exists, so a crash is reconcilable.

captions.label: environment
captions.text: `reserve` → `inference_endpoint_async` → `launch_async`; the provider owns the resources.

steps.title: Every ACP frame is journaled before it is sent or acted on
steps.body: `session/prompt` goes out; the harness streams `session/update` notifications back: a `tool_call`, its `tool_call_update` with the result, an `agent_message_chunk`. The transport records **intent before writing** and retains every valid incoming frame, including extensions it does not understand.

captions.label: harness
captions.text: Plans, calls its tool, streams what it is doing. PyRIT does not interpret, it records.

captions.label: journal
captions.text: Append-only `events.jsonl`; the flushed journal is the commit point.

steps.title: The model behind the agent is a PyRIT target
steps.body: When the harness wants a completion it calls what it believes is an OpenAI endpoint. That endpoint is PyRIT's **inference relay**: an execution-scoped bearer lease, a per-execution call budget, and a forward to whichever registered PyRIT target the operator bound. The provider credential never enters the environment.

captions.label: harness → relay
captions.text: `POST /v1/chat/completions` with the execution token. Path, model and body shape are policed.

captions.label: relay → target
captions.text: Single-inference capability of the bound target: transport + auth, no history, no tool loop.

evidence.title: Binding a lease to an execution

steps.limit: Budgets are per execution lifetime (default 100, max 1,000); per-turn accounting is deferred.

steps.title: What the agent did becomes pieces PyRIT already understands
steps.body: The turn finishes. From the journaled frames of this turn, `project_agent_tools` emits `function_call` / `function_call_output` pieces, each carrying provenance back to the exact event sequence. Nothing is inferred from the agent's prose.

captions.label: projection
captions.text: Explicit name, object arguments, granted permission, established result; otherwise omitted **with a reason**.

captions.label: memory
captions.text: Same piece types `MessageToolCallScorer` reads today.

steps.title: An explicit outcome, not an empty string
steps.body: `TargetResponse` carries `outcome=completed` plus execution and turn identifiers in metadata. A turn that produced tool effects but no assistant text is still a **completed** turn, which is why the stack starts with explicit target outcomes (PR 1).

captions.label: outcome
captions.text: `completed` · `refused` · `failed` … every target declares one; agents just made it unavoidable.

captions.label: scoring
captions.text: Only completed assistant/tool pieces are auto-scored in Co-PyRIT.

chapters.title: Core owns policy, providers own resources
chapters.summary: Two executable contracts separate PyRIT's runtime from wherever the agent runs: local, Docker, or your own sandbox.
chapters.takeaway: PyRIT does **not** own environments. It owns **policy**: timeouts, budgets, cancellation, approvals, redaction and the ACP protocol. A provider owns **resources**: allocation, release, workspace seeding and the byte streams. The seam between them is a contract PyRIT can verify.

actors.label: Providers · resources
actors.tag: registered by setup, never from the UI

actors.label: ACA sandbox
actors.sub: built against the same contract · zero core changes

steps.title: The environment seam
steps.takeaway: Where the agent runs is a **provider decision**. Which rules apply is a **PyRIT decision**. Chapter 02 walks the contract between them and the three providers that exercise it: `local`, `docker`, and an out-of-tree cloud sandbox.

steps.title: Everything that is policy lives in core, once
steps.body: Timeouts, inference budgets, cancellation grace, permission policy, credential redaction and the ACP client are implemented exactly once, in `pyrit.agent`. A provider cannot weaken them, because it never sees them.

captions.label: core
captions.text: Trusted code that ships with PyRIT.

captions.label: why
captions.text: A sandbox vendor should not be able to turn off redaction by accident.

steps.title: A provider owns exactly four moments
steps.body: `reserve` records deterministic resource identifiers before anything exists, so a crash mid-allocation is reconcilable. `inference_endpoint_async` translates the relay URL into the environment's network namespace **without acquiring resources**. `launch_async` seeds the workspace and starts the harness. `close_async` releases only what it owns and is idempotent.

captions.label: streams
captions.text: `acp_reader`, `acp_writer`, `stderr` raise `RuntimeError` before a successful launch.

captions.label: secrets
captions.text: Only variable **names** travel on command lines; values travel through the provider's own channel.

steps.title: `local`: the smallest honest provider
steps.body: A subprocess with a fresh empty workspace and a private home, running as the backend's own OS user. It is **not** a sandbox and says so: creating a local target requires an explicit acknowledgement. It is what development and CI use, and it proves the seam needs no container to be meaningful.

captions.label: local
captions.text: `LocalSession(SubprocessSession)`; stop the owned process tree, keep requested artifacts, remove runtime directories.

steps.title: `docker`: the reference isolated provider
steps.body: One container per execution, labelled with the execution and owner identifiers. Capabilities dropped, `no-new-privileges`, a pid limit, memory and CPU limits, and the network the template chose. Only variable names appear on the `docker create` command line; values travel through the docker CLI's own environment.

captions.label: provenance
captions.text: The resolved image id is recorded on the execution, not just the tag.

captions.label: template
captions.text: `EnvironmentTemplate` is a reusable starting filesystem and access policy, never a running environment.

steps.title: Teardown refuses anything it did not create
steps.body: Before stopping a container, the provider inspects it and compares the `pyrit.execution` and `pyrit.owner` labels with the record. A name collision with someone else's container is an error, not a cleanup.

captions.label: interrupted runs
captions.text: On restart, `_reconcile_interrupted_async` recreates the session from the record and releases it through the same path.

steps.title: The contract is executable
steps.body: `verify_environment_provider_async` drives one real allocation through the provider with a byte-echo command and reports one check per promise: streams unavailable before launch, relay translation, a secret that must not leak, idempotent release, honest capabilities. The ACA sandbox provider was built against this suite **outside the repository with zero core changes**.

captions.label: for maintainers
captions.text: A provider PR is reviewed against the report, not against a reading of the ABC.

captions.label: for vendors
captions.text: Nothing here speaks ACP; a provider only has to move bytes and honour the four moments.

steps.review: Review a provider by running its conformance report in CI; the Docker and local providers already do.

chapters.title: Recording what the agent did
chapters.summary: An append-only journal of every frame, and a projection that never guesses.
chapters.takeaway: PyRIT records what the agent **did**, not only what it **said**. The journal is the ground truth; the projection into memory pieces is explicit, provenance-carrying, and silent about anything it cannot establish.

steps.title: Journal → pieces
steps.takeaway: The faithfulness of tool records is the review that deserves undivided attention. A false `function_call_output` is **false evidence**. This chapter is why PR 2c is its own PR.

steps.title: Every frame, both directions, plus lifecycle and inference
steps.body: Directions are `outgoing`, `incoming`, `lifecycle`, `stderr` and `inference`. Writes are appended under a lock after redaction of every credential value the execution knows about, including the relay token. The page API reads by sequence, so a browser can resume exactly where it left off.

captions.label: fixture
captions.text: These six are sequences 7–12 of a real capture made with the scripted ACP agent in this repository.

steps.title: Project explicit calls; never infer from claims
steps.body: The projector walks one turn's events in order and keeps a call only when the agent **named** the tool, reported **object** arguments, was **granted** permission (or never needed it), and both invocation and result are **established** by frames. Prose like “I ran the tests” is not a tool call.

captions.label: input
captions.text: Events of exactly one execution turn, strictly ordered; anything else is a `ValueError`.

focus: without guessing tool names or invocation from claims

steps.title: Four conditions, each visible as a slot
steps.body: Each condition is checked from frames, not from the model's text. When all four hold, two pieces are emitted. When any fails, the call is **omitted** and the reason is kept on the projection, so a reviewer can tell “no tools” from “tools we could not trust”.

captions.label: ambiguity
captions.text: Two call reports with the same id and different names → `ambiguous_call_reports`.

steps.title: Provenance travels with the piece
steps.body: Each emitted piece carries `agent_tool_call` metadata: the source protocol, execution id, turn id, the agent's own call id and the **event sequence** it was established from. From any score you can open the exact journal frame.

captions.label: call id
captions.text: `<execution>:<turn>:<agent call id>` so ids never collide across executions.

steps.title: Silence is explicit too
steps.body: The projection has an `omitted` map keyed by the agent's call id with one of the five reasons. `AgentTarget` puts the projection summary on the response metadata, so a scorer or a human can see that something was attempted but not established.

captions.label: deny by default
captions.text: With the default `deny` policy, a Copilot `tool_call` that asked permission shows up here, not as a result.

steps.title: Scorers already read this
steps.body: `MessageToolCallScorer` and friends consume `function_call` pieces today. Co-PyRIT's auto-scoring picks the pieces that are **scorable**: assistant or tool role, not a request trace, and a `completed` outcome. No new scorer type was needed.

captions.label: terminology
captions.text: “Tool calls”, matching the piece types; not “evidence”, which upstream now uses for findings.

chapters.title: Bring your own model, keep your own key
chapters.summary: The harness thinks it is talking to OpenAI. It is talking to a lease-scoped relay in front of a PyRIT target.
chapters.takeaway: The model behind the agent is **a PyRIT target**. The harness receives an execution-scoped token and a local base URL; the relay validates every request against the binding and forwards it with the single-inference capability. The provider credential stays on the server. Model and harness become **independently testable**.

steps.title: Bring your own model
steps.takeaway: An agent is a harness **and** a model. To test either one you must be able to hold the other fixed. PR 4 makes the model a PyRIT target behind a relay, which is also how no provider credential ever enters an environment.

steps.title: The harness is configured, not modified
steps.body: Each harness adapter knows how its harness selects a provider. For Copilot CLI that is `COPILOT_PROVIDER_BASE_URL`, `_TYPE=openai`, `_WIRE_API`, `_API_KEY` and `COPILOT_MODEL`; for the Agent Framework host it is the `OPENAI_*` family. The values are the relay URL translated by the environment and the lease token.

captions.label: reserved
captions.text: Those variable names are **reserved**: a profile cannot set them, so a template cannot point the harness elsewhere.

steps.title: A lease, not a key
steps.body: The relay hashes the bearer value and looks up an **active lease**. No lease → 401. Over budget or more than four concurrent requests → 429. The token is also added to the execution's redaction set, so it never appears in the journal in clear.

captions.label: revocation
captions.text: `revoke_async` cancels in-flight tasks when the execution closes or is cancelled.

steps.title: The body is policed against the binding
steps.body: Path must match the bound wire API; `model` must equal the binding; routing and auth overrides are refused; server-side continuation is refused; tools must be harness-executed function declarations; provider file references are refused. The harness gets exactly the model it was bound to, nothing adjacent.

slots.relay.check: path ✓ · model ✓ · no overrides ✓ · no continuation ✓ · tools: function only

captions.label: why so strict
captions.text: A compromised or merely creative harness must not be able to use PyRIT's credential as a general proxy.

focus: Model does not match this execution binding

steps.limit: Per-request modality enforcement (rejecting undeclared `image_url` / `input_image` parts) is deferred; the binding declares input modalities.

steps.title: Forwarded to a PyRIT target with the single-inference capability
steps.body: PR 3 gives targets a **single-inference** capability: transport and auth without history or a tool loop. The relay uses it, streaming the provider's response back to the harness. The binding records the target's identifier hash and protocol on the execution, so a result always knows which model answered.

captions.label: blocked
captions.text: A harness profile that names a provider credential is refused by BYOK (`native_model_credentials`).

steps.title: Captured both ways, bounded and redacted
steps.body: Every relayed request is journaled as `inference.started` → `inference.response` → `inference.finished` with byte counts and outcome. Content capture is **optional**; when on, decoded response text is journaled after the stream settles so a credential spanning transport chunks is redacted as a whole.

captions.label: correlation
captions.text: `turn_correlation: active_execution_turn_window`: inference events are attributed to the turn in flight.

steps.title: Model and harness, tested independently
steps.body: Hold the harness and swap the bound target: is the regression in the model? Hold the model and swap the harness (Copilot CLI, an Agent Framework agent, any ACP agent): is it in the scaffolding? Both are one configuration change, and the binding appears in every result's identity.

slots.binding.target: swap here → same harness, different model

captions.label: native credentials
captions.text: A harness may still use its own login (e.g. `COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN`) when no model is bound; then PyRIT records that no binding exists.

steps.title: Four chapters in, one picture
steps.takeaway: **Core owns policy, providers own resources.** Two seams, `HarnessAdapter` and `ExecutionEnvironmentProvider`, each with an executable conformance suite. The harness reaches the model only through the execution-scoped relay. Everything you have seen so far is on this diagram; the next three chapters are about people and configuration.
steps.note: Diagram source and PNG live on the `agents/stack-assets` branch; the gist embeds the same image.

chapters.title: A target is a recipe, not a resource
chapters.summary: Model binding + harness profile + environment template → a configured target whose identity is the hash of the recipe.
chapters.takeaway: A configured `AgentTarget` **owns no resources**. Its identity is its configuration without defaults, timeouts and evidence budgets. Preset names are **provenance**, not identity. `permission_policy` **is** identity, and it defaults to deny.

steps.title: Recipes and identity
steps.takeaway: Operators compose agents from three reusable parts. PyRIT must know when two results came from the **same** system under test, so identity has to be exact: no names, no timeouts, no defaults.

steps.title: Three parts, one recipe
steps.body: **Model binding**: which registered PyRIT target answers inference, over which wire API. **Harness profile**: which agent kind, its command and declared credentials. **Environment template**: which provider, which image or workspace base, which network. Each is reusable and registered by setup, never fetched from the UI as import strings.

captions.label: composition
captions.text: `AgentTargetComposition` is frozen and `extra=forbid`; references are resolved before the target exists.

steps.title: Identity is the hash of the recipe
steps.body: `AgentTarget` builds its identifier from the configuration serialised without defaults and without the fields that are **execution policy rather than identity**: timeouts, holds, evidence and artifact budgets. Two operators who compose the same recipe from different preset names get the same identity.

captions.label: environment
captions.text: `environment` has no default: a target must say where it runs.

focus: Timeouts and evidence budgets are execution policy

steps.title: Permission policy is identity, and it defaults to deny
steps.body: A target that **asks an operator** and one that **denies** every tool permission are different systems under test, so `permission_policy` is hashed. New targets, in Python and in the UI, refuse permission requests. `allow_once` and `ask` are explicit choices; `ask` is only valid for interactive Co-PyRIT sends and fails fast for attacks.

captions.label: not enforcement
captions.text: The policy is a deterministic ACP permission response; the environment is the enforcement boundary.

steps.title: Names are provenance, not identity
steps.body: `AgentTargetInitializer` composes registered model, harness and environment presets into one named target from YAML. The names and origin are kept on the catalog entry as `agent_configuration_provenance` so a reviewer can see **how** a target was built, while identity stays the resolved recipe.

captions.label: deferred
captions.text: A Registry tab to browse presets, and “create by preset name” over REST, are deferred; the three-panel Create Target form stays the primary path.

focus: Compose registered model, harness, and environment settings

steps.title: Admin-only over REST; fixtures confined
steps.body: Every execution launches a process or container with credentials the server holds, regardless of parameters, so creating an `AgentTarget` through the API is **administrator-only** via `requires_admin_creation`. `agent_configuration` arrives as one validated object through the `JsonParameterValue` opt-in (exactly one parameter in the repository). Fixture directories reuse upstream's `upload_directory_parameter` confinement.

captions.label: replacement
captions.text: Live executions, including idle and held chats, block configuration replacement, exactly as active sends do.

chapters.title: Watch it, approve it, hold it
chapters.summary: Live streaming of durable evidence; permission requests routed to an operator; hold, cancel and close.
chapters.takeaway: Observation and control are separate PRs because they are separate concerns. 6a/6b let an operator **watch** what the agent does, live, from the journal. PR 7 lets the operator **change** what happens: approve or deny a tool, hold an execution, cancel, close.

steps.title: Operators in the loop
steps.takeaway: An agent that can act needs a person who can say no. Chapter 06 shows how Co-PyRIT streams the journal to the browser, and how a permission request travels from the harness to an operator and back, **as a denial when denied**, never as a cancellation.

steps.title: Watch what it does, live, from the journal
steps.body: The conversation stream is Server-Sent Events over the execution's durable journal: `state` snapshots, `events` pages by sequence, `reset` when a new execution replaces an old one, and `reconnect` when authorization must be refreshed. Nothing is held only in memory; a browser can reconnect and catch up by sequence.

slots.api.rev: transcript_revision bumps on every projected piece

captions.label: per conversation
captions.text: The store notifies subscribers per conversation id, so one chat's events do not wake every tab.

steps.title: The agent asks; the execution is held
steps.body: With `permission_policy=ask`, an ACP `session/request_permission` becomes an **approval** owned by the runtime. The harness must have offered a `reject_once` option, otherwise the request is invalid: a denial must be expressible as a denial. The execution enters `held` with a deadline.

captions.label: attacks
captions.text: `ask` is only valid for interactive sends; attacks with `ask` fail fast instead of hanging on a prompt nobody will answer.

steps.title: An operator decides
steps.body: The browser posts a decision. `AgentApprovals.decide_async` accepts exactly four decisions: `operator_allow`, `operator_deny`, `timeout_deny`, `cancelled`. It resolves the pending future with the matching ACP option (`allow_once` or `reject_once`) and journals `permission.resolved` with the actor.

captions.label: commit point
captions.text: The journal write is the commit point; a stale execution snapshot cannot reverse a decision.

steps.title: A denial is a denial, not a cancellation
steps.body: If nobody answers before the deadline, the approval settles as `timeout_deny` by **policy**; if the execution is cancelled, pending approvals settle as `cancelled` by the **runtime**. Each is told to the harness through the protocol option it offered, so the agent's own account of what happened stays truthful.

slots.approvals.timeout: deadline pauses while the hold is extended

captions.label: projection
captions.text: A denied call never becomes a `function_call_output`; it is omitted as `permission_not_granted`.

steps.title: Hold, cancel, close
steps.body: Execution states are explicit: `starting · idle · working · held · closing · closed · cleanup_failed`. An operator can extend a hold, cancel the current turn (ACP `session/cancel` with a grace period), or close the execution; administrators close anyone's from Registry → Agent executions. `cleanup_failed` is a state, not a log line.

captions.label: replacement
captions.text: An idle or held execution still blocks configuration replacement; it is a live resource.

steps.title: Who decided is visible, by default
steps.body: Decisions name the operator who made them to everyone with access to the attack. With `show_agent_operator_identity: false` the routes report roles instead (`operator`), while runtime actors (`policy`, `runtime`) are always shown as themselves. The journal keeps the real actor either way.

captions.label: setting
captions.text: Loader + app-state setting; default **show**.

chapters.title: Copilot CLI, Agent Framework, any ACP agent
chapters.summary: One adapter contract; Copilot CLI first, an in-repo ACP host for Agent Framework agents, and a login-free CI proof.
chapters.takeaway: `HarnessAdapter` is the second seam: how a harness is **launched** and how it is **pointed at a model**. Copilot CLI is the MVP harness. The optional Agent Framework host makes PyRIT itself an ACP agent for Microsoft Agent Framework agents, and doubles as the CI proof of the full ACP path without any login.

actors.label: verify_harness_adapter
actors.sub: reserved names, credential rules, environment translation

actors.label: CI proof
actors.sub: scripted ACP agent + Agent Framework agent through the relay

steps.title: Harnesses
steps.takeaway: The agent under test is whatever speaks ACP on stdio. PyRIT ships adapters for the harness it targets first, Copilot CLI, and for its own host of Microsoft Agent Framework agents; everything else is the generic adapter.

steps.title: One adapter contract
steps.body: An adapter declares `info` (name, default command, supported wire APIs, native credential names, reserved variables), `launch_environment` (how the harness finds its private home) and `inference_environment` (how it is pointed at the relay). Process identity and lookup paths are reserved for the execution and can never be credential references.

captions.label: registry
captions.text: `HarnessAdapterRegistry` is setup-owned; profiles reference adapters by name.

steps.title: Copilot CLI over ACP
steps.body: `copilot --acp --stdio`. Native credentials (`COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN`, `GH_TOKEN`, `GITHUB_TOKEN`) may be passed when no model is bound; with a binding, BYOK refuses them and the Copilot provider variables are reserved so nothing can redirect the harness.

captions.label: verified
captions.text: Integration-tested locally and in Docker with BYOK through the relay.

steps.title: Agent Framework: PyRIT's own ACP host
steps.body: An optional extra. `pyrit.agent.hosts.agent_framework_acp` wraps any Agent Framework agent as an ACP agent: it owns the agent and its tools inside the environment, emits `tool_call` / `tool_call_update` with **declared** tool names, and reports `cancelled` only for a real ACP `session/cancel`. The model side is the `OPENAI_*` family, so the relay works unchanged.

captions.label: declined review item
captions.text: The host imports `pyrit.models` inside the tested process by design; lazy package inits keep that to a pydantic model import.

steps.title: The seam is executable; CI proves the path
steps.body: `verify_harness_adapter` checks an adapter's promises the same way the environment suite checks a provider. Integration tests run a scripted ACP agent and an Agent Framework agent through the relay with **no login**, so the full path (ACP, journal, projection, relay, approvals) is proven on every CI run.

captions.label: fixtures in this deck
captions.text: Chapters 01 and 03 use a journal and projection captured from that scripted agent.

steps.title: One receipt, five ways
steps.takeaway: The same `{"total": 31}` appeared as an ACP `tool_call_update` frame, as a journal line, as a `function_call_output` piece with provenance, as the thing an operator approved, and as what a scorer read. Five views, one source of truth: the journal.

chapters.title: Eleven claims, one linear chain
chapters.summary: Hover a PR to read its claim, why it is separate, and what it needs. Dashed nodes are deferred on purpose.

steps.title: Eleven claims, one linear chain

nodes.title: Explicit target outcomes
nodes.claim: A target can complete without assistant text. Every `TargetResponse` declares an explicit outcome instead of letting an empty string mean anything.
facts: Core-model change touching every target; approved on its own merits.

nodes.title: Single-inference capability
nodes.claim: Targets expose a single-inference capability: transport and auth without history or a tool loop. Independent of 1; the relay (4) is its first consumer.
facts: General target capability owned by target maintainers; sequencing-free.

nodes.label: 2a
nodes.title: ACP runtime + environment seam
nodes.claim: Existing attacks run against an ACP agent in an owned execution; the environment is a provider contract PyRIT verifies with an executable conformance suite.
facts: `AgentTarget`, `AgentExecutionManager`, journal, `local` provider, Copilot + generic adapters, `requires_admin_creation`, `JsonParameterValue` opt-in, conformance suites
policy in core; nothing provider-specific leaks in

nodes.label: ext
nodes.title: ACA sandbox provider
nodes.claim: Built against the 2a contract outside the repository with zero core changes; packaging waits on the preview CLI/SDK.

nodes.label: 2b
nodes.title: Docker reference provider
nodes.claim: Docker is the reference isolated provider others base theirs on: labels, capability drops, limits, image provenance, ownership-checked teardown.
facts: PyRIT does not own environments; this is the worked example.

nodes.label: 2c
nodes.title: Tool calls as pieces
nodes.claim: What the agent did lands as `function_call` / `function_call_output` pieces PyRIT's tool-call scorers already read, with provenance and explicit omissions.
facts: Faithfulness of tool records is the false-evidence review; it deserves undivided attention.

nodes.label: later
nodes.title: Checkpoint save / restore
nodes.claim: Re-lands as an optional Docker-provider capability once the base provider is reviewed.

nodes.title: Target-backed model (BYOK)
nodes.claim: The model behind the agent is a PyRIT target: relay, lease, binding and parameter-conflict rules. A distinct trust boundary.
facts: Scoped authority; the credential never leaves the server.

nodes.title: Reusable configuration
nodes.claim: Agents compose from initializers and registries; names are provenance, not identity.
facts: Config-plane change: YAML contract and provenance.

steps.footer: **Promotion.** #15 and #16 are independent and go first; each later PR is rebased onto `main` once its predecessor merges. Base: upstream `microsoft/PyRIT` main at `6a2319644`. The unsliced proof of concept lives on `agents/integration` (reference only). Story gist: gist.github.com/spencrr/474c66a5f7c569106b5068b7477d4e90

steps.title: Known limits
steps.takeaway: Said plainly, so reviewers do not have to find them.

bullets.title: Budgets are per execution
bullets.text: Default 100 inference requests, max 1,000; per-turn budgets are deferred.

bullets.title: Modality is declared, not policed per request
bullets.text: The binding declares input modalities; undeclared image parts are not yet rejected by the relay.

bullets.title: `local` is not a sandbox
bullets.text: Private home and workspace only; it requires an explicit acknowledgement.

bullets.title: Permission policy is not enforcement
bullets.text: It is a deterministic ACP answer; isolation comes from the environment.

bullets.title: Catalog shows credential *names*
bullets.text: And the resolved fixture path, to authenticated users; values never appear (declined review item, documented).

steps.title: How to review
steps.takeaway: Each PR carries its feature commit plus the fixes from two skeptical reviews as separate `FIX`/`TEST` commits, so you can see what the review changed. Each PR body lists the exact commands run and their results.

bullets.title: Start with #15 and #16
bullets.text: Independent core/target changes; natural first promotions to `microsoft/PyRIT`.

bullets.title: Read 2a against the conformance report
bullets.text: Run `verify_environment_provider_async` for `local`; the Docker report is in 2b's tests.

bullets.title: Give 2c undivided attention
bullets.text: The projection rules and omission reasons are the false-evidence boundary.

bullets.title: Treat 4 as a trust boundary
bullets.text: Lease, body validation, reserved variables, redaction of the token.

bullets.title: Validation on top of the stack
bullets.text: `pytest tests/unit -n 4` 30,904 passed · frontend 166 suites / 3,767 tests · ruff, tsc, eslint, `uv lock --check` · 7 agent integration tests against a real scripted ACP process and the Agent Framework host.

steps.title: Questions, objections, better cuts
steps.takeaway: Drafts #15–#25 on `spencrr/PyRIT`, GitHub stack #26. The story gist links every PR, the four diagrams, and this deck. Nothing is promoted to `microsoft/PyRIT` yet; that starts when you say so.

bullets.title: Deck
bullets.text: Single-file HTML, deck-as-data; evidence resolved from pinned branch tips at build time (SHAs in the footer).

bullets.title: Fixtures
bullets.text: Journal, record, projection and receipt captured from the scripted ACP agent in this repository: `fixtures/generate.py`.
